summary: The original is an animated RGB clock — red seconds hand sweeping exactly 6 deg/s (60.0 s/rev) plus green/blue hands — while the port renders a static, byte-identical-for-600 s aliased rainbow/checkerboard wash with no hands and no rotation in any tested dial configuration.
observations: Rig: default grid 16x16, 256 px. Both sides compile and run with no compile/runtime error; neither binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both).

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: orig exposes 8 sliders RadiusMode, HandMode, Sharpness, Strength, Breathe, Speed, Distance, **SecondsBrightness**; port exposes the same 7 plus **SubSecondBrightness**. Eighth control name differs (SecondsBrightness vs SubSecondBrightness); same kind (slider).

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS, structure: orig is sparse (meanBrightness avg 7) — a clock centred on the grid with three saturated hands emanating from centre: green peak (0,255,27) at rows 2-3 col 7-8, blue peak (0,0,164) at rows 4-6 col 7-8, a long red arc reaching rows 0-1 and columns 9-11, plus a dim white/grey marker (values 8-20) at rows 9-11 col 7-8. Port is dense (meanBrightness avg 29, ~4.2x brighter) — a full-width rainbow of ~7 hue cycles banded by row, left/right MIRROR-SYMMETRIC about the vertical centre line (col 0 == col 15, col 1 == col 14 ...), i.e. no angular structure at all, occupying rows 0-8 and black below.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS, motion — the headline finding. Orig: red seconds hand rotates CLOCKWISE at exactly 45 deg per 7.5 s. Measured brightest-red-pixel angle (atan2 about grid centre) at t=0/7.5/15/22.5/30/37.5/45/52.5/60/67.5 s = 356/51/86/135/184/231/274/321/356/51 deg — a clean 60.0 s revolution that repeats (t=60 == t=0, t=67.5 == t=7.5). Port: the same measurement returns (6,3), angle 342 deg, value 234 at EVERY one of those ten times — zero rotation.

PORT IS LITERALLY FROZEN at defaults: a --dump at t=2, 30, 90, 300 and 599 s (600 s run, 2 fps) gives five BYTE-IDENTICAL frames on the port (sha 33137e7c95 x5) while all five orig frames differ. survey-600 stats: port zeroMotionFrames 1195/1200; the only non-zero motion is a 5-frame warm-up transient in the first ~1 s. Orig posts motion >= 1 on 299/300 survey frames.

Rhythm images confirm it: orig-rhythm over 600 s at 2 fps shows 10 clean zigzag traverses (= 60 s/sweep) of the red hand plus a slow green/blue drift (minute/hour hands advancing); port-rhythm over the same 600 s is perfectly flat vertical bands, no structure whatsoever.

WALL-CLOCK ENGINE GAP (pixelclock precedent): --wall-clock 1756000000 / 1756010000 / 1756027200 / 1756041600 produced BYTE-IDENTICAL orig.png (71b1f782b329) and port.png (89aca296b76d) at all four instants. Time-of-day mapping (hour/minute hand placement vs real time, 12h vs 24h, timezone) is therefore UNVERIFIABLE on either side and is excluded from this verdict — hence the confidence cap. Note however that the engine DOES advance a sub-minute time source (the orig's seconds hand rotates), so the port's total freeze is not explained by the pinned clock alone.

DIALED COMPARISON (all seven shared sliders pinned to 0.5, eighth pinned to 0.5 under each side's own name), 12 s @ 10 fps: orig draws a large smooth coloured disc with a blue bar and a red sweep rotating around it (meanBrightness 76, motion 8); port draws a coarse red/green/yellow CHECKERBOARD of ~1 px period (meanBrightness 20, motion 1). Over 180 s at 5 fps the orig's brightness autocorrelation peaks hard at lag 330 frames (66 s, the hand sweep; peak power 121) while the port's top peak is lag 149 frames with power 1.69 — i.e. noise, no periodic structure.

RadiusMode=0 (others 0.5) is the most diagnostic mode: orig draws clean CONCENTRIC RGB RINGS — column x=7 top-to-bottom reads red / green / green-cyan / blue / red / green / green / blue, a ~4-row ring period, and row y=7 is lit edge-to-edge with the same ring sequence. Port at the identical setting draws the SAME COLOURS at roughly the same 4-row vertical period but its row y=7 is black except three centre pixels — the lit region is a jagged scalloped band across the top rather than a disc, and it reads as a 1-px-period RGB dither on screen. Structure is aliased/wrong even where the palette is right.

RadiusMode=1: orig draws a smooth white/cyan/red angular WEDGE that rotates over the window; port draws a white field with a high-frequency SAWTOOTH boundary — same colours, spatial frequency far too high.

HandMode=1 is the clearest failure: orig draws four distinct straight hands (red, green, blue and white) radiating from centre at different angles and visibly rotating; port draws a red/green checkerboard mush with NO blue channel present and no identifiable hands.

Brightness is off in BOTH directions: untouched, port is 4.2x too bright (29 vs 7); at every dialed setting tested, port is 2-4x too DIM (dialed-mid 20 vs 76; Sharpness=1 13 vs 68; Strength=0 4 vs 19; Strength=1 53 vs 151).

Aliveness across dial states (8 s @ 10 fps, zeroMotionFrames out of 80): orig 1/80 in every state except Strength=1 (70/80, saturated); port 79/80 (Breathe=0), 72/80 (Speed=1), 61/80 (Sharpness=1), 55/80 (Strength=0), 42/80 (Distance=1), 37/80 (Distance=0), 34/80 (Speed=0), 22/80 (Strength=1), 21/80 (Breathe=1), 20/80 (HandMode=0), 4/80 (Sharpness=0), 1/80 (HandMode=1). The port is near-frozen in most modes and only genuinely animates under HandMode=1 and Sharpness=0 — and even there the motion is a per-frame flicker, not a rotating hand.
Seed independence: --seed 1234 reproduces the default run exactly on both sides (orig mean 7 motion 1, port mean 29 motion 1) — this pattern is not RNG-driven, so per-pixel comparison is fair.
No harness warnings on any run; provenance stable across all runs (portSha256 7e1d185b17f7, epeSha256 ce47800da5cc, harnessSha256 70c136952047).

dials.name: sliderRadiusMode
dials.origEffect: Mode selector. At 0: clean concentric R/G/B rings filling a disc (mean 40). At 0.5: filled coloured disc with rotating red sweep (mean 76). At 1: smooth rotating white/cyan/red angular wedge, near-saturated (mean 145). Probe maxDelta 16.5 / maxDeltaLit 29.9.
dials.portEffect: Live but the output is wrong in every position: 0 gives a 1-px-period RGB checkerboard with a scalloped top band (mean 44); 0.5 gives a red/green/yellow checkerboard (mean 20); 1 gives a white field with a high-frequency sawtooth boundary (mean 100). Probe maxDelta 40.8 / maxDeltaLit 61.8 — over-responsive relative to orig.

dials.name: sliderHandMode
dials.origEffect: 0 -> broad soft hands, mean 45, gentle motion (motion avg 2.0); 1 -> four crisp straight hands (red/green/blue/white) radiating from centre at distinct angles and rotating, mean 16, motion 3.0. Probe maxDelta 6.5 / maxDeltaLit 20.7.
dials.portEffect: 0 -> checkerboard, mean 21, near-frozen (zmf 20/80); 1 -> red/green checkerboard mush with NO blue channel and no identifiable hands, mean 10, motion 9.0. Hands are never drawn. Probe maxDelta 13.7 / maxDeltaLit 22.8.

dials.name: sliderSharpness
dials.origEffect: Controls edge softness/spread. 0 -> broad soft bright field (mean 116); 1 -> tight crisp features (mean 68) with more frame-to-frame motion (12 vs 6). Probe maxDelta 97.9.
dials.portEffect: Same direction on brightness (0 -> 70, 1 -> 13) but far more extreme, and it also controls whether the port moves at all: Sharpness=0 is the port's most animated state (zmf 4/80) while Sharpness=1 is near-frozen (zmf 61/80). Probe maxDelta 110.8.

dials.name: sliderStrength
dials.origEffect: Overall intensity/gain. 0 -> dim (mean 19) but still fully animated; 1 -> saturated white-out (mean 151) and effectively frozen (zmf 70/80). Probe maxDelta 176.3 — the strongest dial on the original.
dials.portEffect: Same monotone direction but compressed: 0 -> mean 4, 1 -> mean 53 (orig reaches 151). Probe maxDelta 96.0, roughly half the original's authority.

dials.name: sliderBreathe
dials.origEffect: Probe called it NOT responsive (maxDelta 0.43 / maxDeltaLit 1.35) and the manual 8 s sweep at pinned-mid confirms only a small change (mean 86 at 0 vs 81 at 1, motion 7.8 both). Effect largely unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Probe responsive (maxDelta 7.0 / maxDeltaLit 10.3) and the manual sweep shows it gates the port's ONLY animation: Breathe=0 is fully frozen (zmf 79/80, motion 0.0) while Breathe=1 flickers (zmf 21/80, motion 1.4). The port has invented an on/off animation gate the original does not have.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Probe reported 0.00 delta (inert) over its 4 s window — a false inert. Manual sweep over 8 s with other dials pinned at 0.5 shows a real effect: Speed=0 mean 90 motion 7.5, Speed=1 mean 76 motion 12.0, i.e. it does speed the animation up.
dials.portEffect: Probe 0.00, and the manual sweep confirms it dead where it matters: Speed=0 mean 20.2 motion 0.6 (zmf 34/80), Speed=1 mean 20.6 motion 0.1 (zmf 72/80) — raising Speed makes the port MOVE LESS. Wrong sign and no usable speed control.

dials.name: sliderDistance
dials.origEffect: Probe responsive (maxDelta 7.4 / maxDeltaLit 20.9); manual sweep at pinned-mid shows identical stats at 0 and 1 (mean 83.4, motion 7.8 both) — a geometry/hand-length change that the whole-rig means cannot see. Effect real but only partly characterisable from output.
dials.portEffect: Probe responsive (maxDelta 27.0 / maxDeltaLit 43.0), ~3.6x the original's magnitude; manual sweep changes brightness (17.5 at 0 vs 21.5 at 1) where the original's does not.

dials.name: sliderSecondsBrightness (orig) / sliderSubSecondBrightness (port)
dials.origEffect: NAME DIFFERS BETWEEN SIDES. On the original this is the seconds-hand intensity and it is decisive: 0 -> mean 64 and motion 0 (the moving seconds hand vanishes, leaving a static face); 1 -> mean 136 and motion 28 (bright fast-sweeping hand, the highest motion of any run in this verdict).
dials.portEffect: Renamed to SubSecondBrightness. Probe called it responsive from untouched defaults (maxDelta 12.1 / maxDeltaLit 19.4), but with the other seven dials pinned at 0.5 it is completely inert: 0 and 1 both give mean 20, motion 1. It never produces or suppresses a moving seconds hand, because the port has no moving seconds hand to control.

feedback: PRIMARY: the port's clock never advances. The original's red seconds hand rotates clockwise at exactly 6 deg/s (measured angles 356/51/86/135/184/231/274/321/356 deg at 7.5 s intervals; 60.0 s per revolution, repeating). The port's brightest red feature sits at (6,3), angle 342 deg, value 234, unchanged from t=0 to t=599 s, and five dumped frames spread over 600 s are byte-identical. Whatever time source the port reads for the second/minute/hour angles is returning a constant. NOTE for attribution: the harness engine DOES advance a sub-minute time source (the original proves it), but it pins the absolute wall clock (--wall-clock had zero effect on either side across four values), so first check whether the port reads a clock builtin the engine constant-folds while the original reads one that advances — if so this is an engine gap, not a port bug, and should be filed as such.

SECONDARY: the port draws no hands. The original renders each hand as a localised radial feature at its own angle — at HandMode=1 four crisp straight red/green/blue/white spokes at distinct angles, at defaults a green blob at rows 2-3, a blue blob at rows 4-6 and a long red arc reaching column 11. The port's output is left/right MIRROR-SYMMETRIC about the vertical centre line at defaults (col 0 == col 15, col 1 == col 14, ...), which is proof it has no angular term at all — it is shading purely on radius. Restore the per-hand angular test.

The port's radial/spatial frequency is far too high — roughly an order of magnitude. At RadiusMode=0 the original lays down R/G/B rings with a ~4-row period across a filled disc; the port lays the same colours down as a ~1 px dither/checkerboard. At RadiusMode=1 the original's smooth angular wedge becomes a high-frequency sawtooth on the port. This smells like a radius (or angle) expressed in raw pixel units where the original uses a 0..1 normalised value, or a missing divide by the canvas half-width. Fixing the normalisation should collapse most of the checkerboard artefacts.

The lit REGION shape is wrong. At RadiusMode=0 the original fills row y=7 edge to edge (a disc); the port lights only the three centre pixels of that row and instead paints a scalloped band across rows 0-8. Whatever radius/distance test decides which pixels are inside a ring is producing an inverted-V region rather than an annulus.

Brightness calibration is off in both directions and should be checked after the geometry is fixed: untouched the port is 4.2x too bright (mean 29 vs 7 — it floods the canvas where the original lights only a few hands); at every dialed setting it is 2-4x too dim (dialed-mid 20 vs 76, Strength=1 53 vs 151).
sliderSpeed has the wrong sign on the port: raising it from 0 to 1 DROPS the port's motion (zeroMotionFrames 34/80 -> 72/80) where it raises the original's (motion 7.5 -> 12.0).

sliderBreathe has become an animation on/off gate on the port (Breathe=0 -> 79/80 frozen frames, Breathe=1 -> 21/80) — on the original it is a subtle modulation with no effect on whether the pattern moves (motion 7.8 at both ends). Breathe should not be gating the clock's motion.

Rename the eighth control back to the original's `sliderSecondsBrightness` (label `SecondsBrightness`). The port calls it `sliderSubSecondBrightness` (label `SubSecondBrightness`), so a saved preset or any --controls string written against the original silently no-ops. On the original this dial is the seconds-hand intensity: at 0 the moving hand disappears entirely (motion drops to 0) and at 1 it is the brightest, fastest element on the canvas (motion 28); the port must reproduce that once the hand animates again.
The port keeps no blue channel at HandMode=1 (the original draws a distinct blue hour hand there) — check that the hour hand is being emitted at all in that mode.

TIME-OF-DAY MAPPING IS UNVERIFIED and cannot be checked with the current harness: --wall-clock at 1756000000, 1756010000, 1756027200 and 1756041600 produced byte-identical renders on BOTH sides. Once the port's hands move again, hour/minute placement vs real time (12h vs 24h dial, direction, zero-angle convention, timezone) still needs a separate check on hardware or after the engine clock gap is closed.
